summary: Lets the least-privilege PostgreSQL schema-epoch preflight verify existing tables and RLS policies without business-data access.
userImpact: Pooled PostgreSQL upgrades no longer reject a ready schema because the dedicated preflight login cannot see protected tables through information_schema.

instructions: Deploy the matching backend image and host chart through the normal migration and schema-epoch preflight sequence.

notes: No schema, policy, role, or grant is changed; verification reads PostgreSQL system catalogs and the signed migration ledger only.

security: The membership-free preflight login retains zero business-table privileges while verifying relation presence and exact RLS policy catalogs.
Generic bootstrap and data-integrity reads remain on application and owner invocations and are excluded from the dedicated schema-epoch preflight.
documentation: The generated technical release notes describe the least-privilege PostgreSQL preflight correction.
rollback: Redeploy the preceding backend image and chart; no database rollback or credential change is required.
validation: Unit tests preserve migration orchestration and verify that the schema-epoch preflight skips business-table inspection.
A PostgreSQL 16 integration test proves the preflight login has no SELECT privilege or information_schema visibility while catalog-backed RLS verification succeeds.
